findings.description: Invite codes are bearer credentials that grant workspace membership. They are generated with `random.choices`, which uses the Mersenne Twister. Its output is predictable once enough outputs are observed, so an attacker who sees a few codes could predict others and join workspaces uninvited.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `"".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))`, or `secrets.token_urlsafe`.
findings.title: Invite codes generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `accept` rejects revoked links and exhausted links but never checks `now >= link.expires_at`. An expired link can still be used to join the workspace, which defeats the TTL. `is_active` already encodes the full rule but is not used here.
findings.title: accept() does not check link expiry

findings.description: The `uses >= max_uses` check, `directory.add`, and `link.uses += 1` are separate steps with no lock. Concurrent accepts of a single-use link can all pass the check and all join, exceeding `max_uses`.
findings.suggestion: Guard accept (check, add, increment) with a lock, or use an atomic increment-and-check.
findings.title: Check-then-act on link usage is not atomic
